```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
```

## Problem 1

Creating a function to simulate birthdays for a group of a given size and determine whether at least two people share a birthday.

```{r birthday}
birthday_simulation = function(n){
  birthday = sample(1:365, size = n, replace = TRUE)
  any(duplicated(birthday))
}
```

Run this function 10000 times for each group size between 2 and 50.

```{r}
birthday_result = 
  expand_grid(
    group_size = 2:50,
    iteration = 1:10000
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    duplicate = map_lgl(group_size, birthday_simulation)
  )
```

Calculated the estimated probability for each group size and plotted the results.

```{r}
birthday_summary = 
  birthday_result |> 
  group_by(group_size) |> 
  summarize(
    probability = mean(duplicate)
  )

birthday_summary |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = group_size, y = probability)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  labs(
    x = "Group Size",
    y = "Probability of Shared Birthday",
    title = "Probability of at Least Two People Sharing a Birthday"
  )
```

Conclusion: The probability of at least two people sharing a birthday increases rapidly as group size increases. The probability is about 0.5 when the group size is around 23 and increases to about 0.97 when the group size reaches 50.



## Problem 2

Created a dataframe containing the file names for all participants.

```{r, message=FALSE}
longitudinal_df = 
  tibble(
    files = list.files("data/"),
    path = str_c("data/", files)
  ) |> 
  mutate(data = map(path, read_csv)) |> 
  unnest(data)
```

Tidied the data by extracting treatment group and subject ID from the file names and converting the weekly observations from wide to long format.

```{r}
tidy_df =
  longitudinal_df |>
  mutate(
    files = str_replace(files, ".csv", ""),
    group = str_sub(files, 1, 3)
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    week_1:week_8,
    names_to = "week",
    values_to = "outcome",
    names_prefix = "week_"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    week = as.numeric(week),
    group = case_match(
    group,
    "con" ~ "Control",
    "exp" ~ "Experimental"
  )
  ) |> 
  select(group, subj = files, week, outcome)
```

Then created a spaghetti plot to show observations on each subject over time.

```{r}
tidy_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = week, y = outcome, group = subj, color = group)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_path() +
  facet_grid(~group) +
  labs(
    x = "Week",
    y = "Outcome",
    title = "Participant Outcomes Over Time"
  )
```

The control group shows relatively little overall change across the eight weeks. In contrast, participants in the experimental group generally show increasing outcome values over time.
